I reviewed my initial assessment against the Self-Reflection Checklist. 

1. Score-Reasoning Consistency: My scores align perfectly with my reasoning. Atoms 3 and 4 received 0.0 because the image fundamentally fails the specific constraints ('two' vs 'clusters', 'striped' vs 'solid center'). The authenticity score of 2.0 reflects the severity of the fusion artifact (severity 4) and text gibberish (severity 3), which are major structural defects.

The fine_grained_classifier correctly identified the vehicle as a scooter but failed to identify the flowers (predicting 'iron'), supporting the verdict that the flowers are malformed/hallucinated. The perceptual_quality_auditor reported 'null' distortion, but I correctly noted in my review that this does not preclude structural artifacts like fusion, which I verified visually.

3. Reference Calibration: No reference images were provided, so I relied on internal calibration. A score of 2.5 alignment is appropriate for an image that gets the main object right but fails specific attribute/count constraints and has severe artifacts.

4. Leniency Bias: I did not rubber-stamp the Router. I independently verified the 'fusion' claim by looking at the handlebar/stem junction and confirmed the text was indeed gibberish rather than a stylized font.

5. Harshness Bias: I ensured the minor texture anomaly (flower centers) did not dominate the score; the low authenticity is driven primarily by the severe fusion and text errors.

6. Atom Score Review: All atom scores are justified. Taxonomy scores are 1.0 as no taxonomy info contradicts the QA pairs themselves (the taxonomy describes daisies, but the prompt asked for 'striped flowers', so the failure is prompt adherence, not taxonomy violation per se).

7. Upward Override Justification: No upward overrides were made. All positive verdicts (motorcycle presence, color, flower presence) were independently verified via visual inspection and expert detection confidence >0.9.

Final scores remain unchanged as they accurately reflect the image quality and prompt adherence.
